close_reason: Closed in single doc pass commit. The new '# Contract guarantees' (or '# Features') section in pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs covers this finding.
description:
pkix-truststore is silent in rustdoc about panic safety. No function says
'this function does not panic on any input.' This is unusual for a Tier-1
parsing library that explicitly defends against an upstream panic in its
own code (see lib.rs:316-329).

Current state:

  - lib.rs:316-323 carries a hand-written guard ('input contains no BEGIN
    boundary -> NoCertificates') specifically to avoid triggering a
    subtract-with-overflow panic in x509-cert 0.2.x's load_pem_chain.
    The comment references RustCrypto/formats#1965 and notes the
    workaround can be removed when the workspace bumps to x509-cert
    0.3.x. PKIX-tit4.6 already discusses this from a duplication angle.
  - There is no statement that all other inputs are panic-free.
  - The crate's `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at lib.rs:2 means no UB, but
    safe Rust can still panic (subtract-with-overflow under debug
    builds, allocation failure, etc.).

What goes wrong for a caller in production:

  - A high-assurance caller (e.g., a TLS server fronting a payments API)
    that must not unwind into uncontrolled crash needs to know whether
    to wrap trust-store loading in catch_unwind. With no documented
    contract, the safe default is to wrap, which adds latency and obscures
    real errors.
  - A library caller composing pkix-truststore into a service-level
    'fail-on-startup' loader cannot tell whether a malformed CA bundle
    will produce a useful Error or a panic that bypasses Result::Err
    handlers.
  - A fuzzer-driven harness needs to know whether to treat panics as
    bugs or as expected behavior on malformed input. Without a contract,
    fuzz triage is ambiguous.

Fix: add a top-level rustdoc section to lib.rs:

  //! # Panic safety
  //!
  //! All loaders in this crate are panic-free on any input: malformed
  //! PEM, malformed DER, truncated input, oversized input, and adversarial
  //! input return `Err(Error::...)` rather than panicking. Allocation
  //! failure follows the standard library policy (`Vec::push` may abort
  //! the process under the global allocator's policy; we do not catch
  //! this).
  //!
  //! Internally we guard against one known panic in
  //! `x509-cert::load_pem_chain` (subtract-with-overflow on empty input
  //! after whitespace strip); see RustCrypto/formats#1965. The guard is
  //! removed when the workspace bumps to `x509-cert 0.3.x`.

This is a contract the maintainer is already keeping (the test suite at
fixtures.rs and serde_round_trip.rs covers every named negative case
without a single `#[should_panic]`). The doc only needs to say it.
title: Panic-safety contract is undocumented; crate already carries one defensive workaround against an upstream panic
